title: Fabrication of molecular tension probes
author: Kim, Fujii
materials: 1.Generate the cDNA segments encoding full-length Renilla luciferase 8 (1–311 aa; RLuc8) by PCR using a corresponding primer set flanked with unique restriction sites, BamHI and KpnI, for introducing unique restriction sites at the 5′- and 3′-terminals, respectively.2.Fabricate the cDNA segments encoding the ER LBD and the SH2 domain of v-Src by PCR using corresponding primer sets flanked with the unique restriction sites, HindIII/BamHI, and KpnI/XhoI, respectively.3.Digest the above cDNA segments and the multiple cloning site (MCS) of a mammalian expression vector pcDNA 3.1(+) (Invitrogen) with the corresponding restriction enzymes, HindIII/BamHI; BamHI/KpnI; KpnI/XhoI; HindIII/KpnI, respectively (Fig. 1B).24.Gel-purify the digested cDNA segments and the mammalian expression vector.5.Ligate the cDNA segments into the expression vector pcDNA 3.1(+) (Invitrogen) to fabricate a cDNA construct encoding the molecular tension probe (single coding sequence) (Fig. 1B).6.Confirm the sequences of the cDNA constructs in pcDNA3.1(+) vector with a genetic sequencer (GenomeLab GeXP, Beckman Coulter) (named pErs).3

steps.title: PCR amplify DNA fragments
steps.instruction: Generate cDNA segments by PCR: (i) full‑length Renilla luciferase 8 (1–311 aa; RLuc8) using primers flanked with BamHI (5′) and KpnI (3′); (ii) estrogen‑receptor ligand‑binding domain (ER LBD) using HindIII/BamHI‑flanked primers; (iii) SH2 domain of v‑Src using KpnI/XhoI‑flanked primers.

steps.title: Digest DNA and vector
steps.instruction: Digest the PCR‑generated cDNA segments and the multiple‑cloning site of pcDNA3.1(+) (Invitrogen) with the appropriate restriction enzymes: HindIII/BamHI for ER LBD, BamHI/KpnI for RLuc8, KpnI/XhoI for SH2, and HindIII/KpnI for the vector backbone.

steps.title: Gel‑purify digested fragments
steps.instruction: Run the digested cDNA segments and the linearized pcDNA3.1(+) vector on an agarose gel and excise the correct bands; purify the DNA fragments from the gel.

steps.title: Ligate fragments into expression vector
steps.instruction: Ligate the purified cDNA fragments into the gel‑purified pcDNA3.1(+) vector to create a single‑coding‑sequence construct encoding the molecular tension probe.

steps.title: Verify construct by sequencing
steps.instruction: Confirm the nucleotide sequence of the assembled construct in pcDNA3.1(+) using a genetic sequencer (GenomeLab GeXP, Beckman Coulter); designate the verified plasmid as pErs.

steps.title: Grow COS‑7 cells in culture
steps.instruction: Culture COS‑7 cells (African green monkey kidney fibroblasts) in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s Medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (Gibco) and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin (Gibco) at 37 °C in a 5 % CO₂ incubator.

steps.title: Transfect cells in 12‑well plates
steps.instruction: Seed COS‑7 cells into 12‑well culture plates and transiently transfect each well with 1 µg of pErs using TransIT‑LT1 (Mirus); incubate for 16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Stimulate and lyse 12‑well cells
steps.instruction: Stimulate the transfected cells for 20 min with either vehicle (0.1 % DMSO), 1 µM 17β‑estradiol (E2), or 1 µM 4‑hydroxytamoxifen (OHT). Wash once with PBS (pH 7.4, 0.02 M). Lyse cells with Promega lysis buffer E291A for 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Measure bioluminescence spectra (12‑well)
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 µL of each lysate into a 200 µL microtube, add 50 µL of assay buffer E290B (Promega) containing native coelenterazine (nCTZ), and immediately record the bioluminescence spectrum with a spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Transfect cells in 96‑well plates
steps.instruction: Seed COS‑7 cells in a 96‑well clear‑bottom microplate until ~70 % confluence; transfect each well with 0.2 µg of pErs using TransIT‑LT1 (Mirus); incubate 16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Stimulate and lyse 96‑well cells
steps.instruction: Stimulate cells for 20 min with vehicle, 10⁻⁶ M E2, or 10⁻⁶ M OHT. Wash once with PBS, then lyse with Promega lysis buffer E291A for 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Measure luminescence with luminometer (96‑well)
steps.instruction: Transfer the lysates to a 1.6 mL microtube, add assay solution E290B (Promega) containing nCTZ, and immediately read bioluminescence intensity using a GloMax 20/20 luminometer (Promega).

steps.title: Quantify protein and normalize luminescence
steps.instruction: Determine total protein in an aliquot of each lysate with Bradford reagent. Normalize RLuc luminescence (RLU) by calculating the ratio RLU(+) / RLU(–), where ‘+’ denotes lysate from ligand‑treated cells and ‘–’ denotes lysate from vehicle‑treated cells; use 1 µg of lysate for each measurement.

steps.title: Alternative plate imaging assay – transfer lysate
steps.instruction: Aliquot 10 µL of each cell lysate into individual wells of a fresh 96‑well optical‑bottom plate.

steps.title: Alternative plate imaging assay – add substrate and image
steps.instruction: Inject 50 µL of assay buffer E290B (Promega) containing nCTZ into each well using a multichannel pipette, then immediately place the plate in a LAS‑4000 image analyzer (FujiFilm).

steps.title: Alternative plate imaging assay – analyze and normalize
steps.instruction: Acquire optical intensities with Image reader ver 2.0, process images using Multi Gauge ver 3.1, and normalize the values (originally expressed as RLU / mm²) to integrated time (seconds) and protein amount (µg) to obtain RLU / µg / sec / mm².

steps.title: Transfect cells in ibidi microslide
steps.instruction: Seed COS‑7 cells in a 6‑channel µ‑slide VI0.4 (ibidi) until ~70 % confluence; transiently transfect each channel with pErs using TransIT‑LT1 (Mirus) and incubate 16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Stimulate, wash, add substrate and image microslide
steps.instruction: Stimulate cells in the channels for 20 min with either vehicle (0.1 % DMSO) or 10⁻⁶ M OHT. Wash once with Hank’s Buffered Salt Solution (HBSS, Gibco) and fill each channel with 80 µL HBSS containing nCTZ using a multichannel pipette. Immediately transfer the slide to a LAS‑4000mini image analyzer (FujiFilm) and capture optical images with Image reader ver 2.0 and Multi Gauge ver 3.1.

description: To date, several potential techniques have been established for determining protein–protein interactions (PPIs), including (i) Bioluminescence resonance energy transfer (BRET) based on energy transfer between bioluminescent donor and fluorescent acceptor proteins [1], [2], [3]; (ii) Mammalian/yeast two-hybrid assay reflecting interactions between “Prey” and “Bait” proteins [4]; (iii) Protein-fragment complementation assay (PCA) making use of split-reporter protein and its conditional reconstitution [5], [6]. We previously developed a unique bioluminescent probe called “strain probe” for illuminating PPIs [7]. We initially hypothesized that any luciferase has talent to change its enzymatic activity according to the molecular tension artificially appended by PPIs. This molecular tension may cause distortion of the active site, which modulates the enzymatic activity. In this method, we introduce how to fabricate molecular tension probes emitting bioluminescence in response to molecular tension appended by PPIs in detail.
